children: India's growth momentum could ease over the next two quarters as government capex spending slows after being front-loaded early in the fiscal year, Goldman Sachs says in a note. "We bake in some sequential moderation...as central government capex growth is likely to decline after front-loading in the first four months of the fiscal year," economists Santanu Sengupta and Arjun Varma write. They note fixed-investment growth reached a four-year high of 11.9% in the April-June quarter and contributed around 4 percentage points to GDP growth. Net exports also provided a further three-point boost as exports surged and imports contracted. GS expects these drivers to moderate sequentially, though strong recent data prompt it to raise its 2026 growth forecast to 7.6% from 7.3%. (jihye.lee@wsj.com)
